articles.title: "Friends with benefits": Zion Williamson finally addresses relationship with se*ual assault accuser in a surprising revelation
articles.summary: NBA News: Zion Williamson has denied the allegations made by a woman who accused him of r*** and se*ual battery, describing their relationship in court document.
articles.body: Zion Williamson has denied the allegations made by a woman who accused him of r*** and se*ual battery, describing their relationship in court documents as a consensual, casual “friends with benefits” arrangement. The New Orleans Pelicans star has issued a general denial of the claims and maintains that he never harmed the woman, identified in the case as Jane Doe.The dispute stems from a civil lawsuit filed in Los Angeles that accuses Williamson of a pattern of abusive and controlling behavior during a relationship that allegedly began while he was at Duke and continued until 2023. Williamson's legal team has rejected those allegations and says the relationship was casual and ended years ago.Zion Williamson's relationship with his se*ual assault accuser revealedZion Williamson's latest position centers on his description of the relationship with Jane Doe. According to the legal documents cited in several reports, including TMZ and Daily Mail, he says the two never dated or lived together and characterized their interactions as “friendly and casual” and consensual. He also disputes the allegations of s*xual assault, battery, and domestic violence.The statement contrasts with the claims made in the lawsuit. Doe alleges that she and Williamson began dating around 2018, when he was playing at Duke, and remained together until 2023. The complaint alleges a broader pattern of physical, emotional and se*ual abuse and describes two alleged r*** incidents after Williamson moved to Beverly Hills during the COVID-19 period. Those are allegations, not established findings in the supplied material.Williamson also disputes the legal basis for some of the claims. His filings reportedly argue that California laws concerning se*ual battery, stalking and domestic violence do not apply to alleged incidents said to have occurred in North Carolina, Texas and Louisiana. He has also described the domestic violence allegation as “nonsensical,” maintaining that the pair never lived together.The case therefore involves two sharply different accounts of the relationship. Doe's complaint portrays it as a long-term relationship marked by alleged coercion and abuse, while Williamson's legal response characterizes it as consensual and casual. The supplied material does not establish the truth of either account.What did Zion Williamson's representatives say?Williamson's attorneys have consistently rejected the allegations. In a statement released in May 2026, his representatives said, “We take these allegations with the utmost seriousness, and we unequivocally deny them. The allegations contained in the complaint are categorically false and reckless.” (via Daily Mail).The statement also challenged the motive behind the lawsuit, saying, “This appears to be an attempt to exploit a professional athlete driven by a financial motive rather than any legitimate grievance.” His attorneys said Williamson and the plaintiff “never dated,” while describing their relationship as consensual and casual. “But did maintain a consensual, casual relationship that began more than six years ago, when he was 18 years old. That relationship ended years ago.”Williamson's representatives further claimed that the plaintiff began demanding millions of dollars following the end of the relationship. “Only after the friendship ended did she begin demanding millions of dollars,” the rep shared. They said Williamson reported what they described as extortion attempts to law enforcement and indicated that he intended to pursue counterclaims and damages over what they called a defamatory lawsuit.The plaintiff's attorneys have rejected that characterization. Sam Taylor of the Lanier Law Firm previously said, “We and our client do not want to litigate this case in the press,” while emphasizing the seriousness of the allegations and saying the plaintiff intended to pursue the case in court.Another attorney for Doe, Rachel Lanier, alleged a pattern of coercive control and threats. “This case shows a disturbing pattern of coercive control, threats, and domination, including stalking, strangulation and threats with a loaded firearm,” she said in the supplied material. “Mr. Williamson used his wealth and fame to isolate, silence and control my client, who only after many months of medical treatment and counseling is able to come forward and describe what she endured,” via Daily Mail.The lawsuit comes amid a turbulent period for WilliamsonThe legal dispute is another off-court issue surrounding Williamson, whose personal life has previously generated significant attention. In 2023, he and Ahkeema Love announced they were expecting a daughter. That announcement was followed by allegations from Moriah Mills, who claimed she had been romantically involved with Williamson and shared alleged private messages.The supplied material also notes that Love was arrested in April in connection with allegations involving another woman romantically linked to Williamson. Police alleged that Love threatened the woman and later attacked her at Williamson's home. The material states that Love was charged with home invasion, aggravated battery and stalking.Those incidents are separate from the civil lawsuit brought by Jane Doe. As per reports, neither woman involved in the Love case is believed to be the plaintiff in the r*** lawsuit.Lindsey Hunter said Zion Williamson needs helpWilliamson's off-court controversies have also drawn commentary from former NBA players. Former Detroit Pistons guard Lindsey Hunter and Hall of Famer Tim Hardaway previously discussed Williamson's career and personal issues, with Hunter making a strong claim about the Pelicans forward's behavior.“He got a problem,” Hunter said in an episode of Crossover Podcast. “The man’s a s*x addict. He’s been caught. He needs help.”Hunter continued, “Why does he keep texting them from his phone? He’s going for like p-rnstars. What is wrong with him? He needs to chill out. They need to give him therapy.”Hunter's comments were commentary rather than a medical diagnosis established in the supplied material. The same material says Williamson has not been involved in any newly reported off-court incidents lately and notes recent footage of him working in the gym.For Williamson, the civil case remains a significant off-court issue as he prepares for another NBA season. articles.title: JJ Redick takes shot at LeBron James, promises starters will not be all 'white guys' in odd presser
articles.summary: JJ Redick made an awkward quip about his Lakers starting lineup's racial makeup while addressing the viral "Snowtime" nickname for Luka Doncic's squad.
articles.body: You can put a podcaster in the head coach's chair, but you still end up with a podcaster. Los Angeles Lakers coach JJ Redick proved as much during his annual news conference Thursday, giving answers better suited for the Twitter timeline than a head coach's seat. First, Redick offered a shady response about the team gelling after superstar LeBron James departed. LEBRON JAMES TELLS LOS ANGELES LAKERS HE WILL LEAVE IN FREE AGENCY AFTER EIGHT SEASONS: REPORT He pointedly noted that this roster has a clearer identity than past squads led by James, his former podcast co-host. "I think we’ve always tried to give our players clearly defined roles, and I think with this group, [it’s] probably the first time in my three years here that I feel like the pieces actually fit together," Redick said. "And so those roles probably get even more crystallized." Since LeBron’s departure, a running joke has taken over Lakers fandom. "Snowtime" has trended across social media as the tongue-in-cheek nickname for the Lakers' projected core of Luka Doncic, Austin Reaves and Walker Kessler — with nods to depth pieces like Dalton Knecht and Maxi Kleber. STEPHEN A SMITH SHOWS HIS PRIVILEGE BY MOCKING LAKERS' ROSTER FOR HAVING TOO MANY 'WHITE DUDES' Because the team's projected top talent isn't Black, the online gag caught fire, and Redick awkwardly addressed it with a questionable remark about his starting unit. Without much context, Redick said he was confident two positions in his lineup would "not be white." "I'm pretty confident in three of the spots," Redick said. "The other two spots will not be two white guys." It was a sarcastic wink to the online crowd, and a cheap internet laugh at best. THE CRAIG CARTON SHOW–UNFILTERED, UNAPOLOGETIC AND UNMISSABLE. DOWNLOAD HIS DAILY PODCAST NOW! Redick now enters his third season at the helm in Los Angeles. His squad was swept in the Western Conference Semifinals by OKC last spring, following a first-round exit against the Minnesota Timberwolves in his inaugural season. Before taking the bench, Redick spent 15 years as an NBA sharpshooter. In 2024, he teamed up with LeBron James to co-host "Mind the Game," a wine-drinking, X's-and-O's basketball podcast. articles.title: Caitlin Clark Posts Career-Low, Box Score Stats, Highlights as Lynx Beat Fever in Season Finale
articles.summary: Caitlin Clark and the Indiana Fever lost playoff seeding ground and Aliyah Boston to injury during Thursday night's regular-season finale.
articles.body:
Caitlin Clark and the Indiana Fever lost playoff seeding ground and Aliyah Boston to injury during Thursday night's regular-season finale.

The Fever will enter the postseason as the WNBA's No. 6 seed after conceding a 86-66 blowout loss to a Minnesota Lynx team missing star rookie Olivia Miles.

Clark recorded career lows in the loss with two points, no three-pointers and 8.3 percent shooting from the field.

Live WNBA Live Updates in Regular Season-Finale

Boston exited the game in the second quarter and was later ruled out with a right lower leg injury.

Here's a look at highlights from a Thursday matchup that will shape the first round of the WNBA postseason.

Shortly after Sophie Cunningham said her team needed to work on faster starts, the Fever recorded one of their slowest first halves of the season against a team that has already clinched the WNBA's top seed.

The Lynx opened scoring with a Maya Caldwell three-pointer, which Clark answered with her lone field goal of the game. The Fever went on to get outscored 21-4 in the opening minutes.

Indiana could not contain the Lynx's three-point shooting as the home team went 11-for-18 from behind the arc through twenty minutes.

The Fever, on the other hand, made three of 21 attempts from deep as the Lynx surged out to a 30-point halftime lead.

Natasha Howard and Kayla McBride had combined for more points (34) than the entirety of the Fever (32) by the break.

The Fever outscored the Lynx 25-10 in the fourth quarter but were unable to make up ground from the early deficit.

Indiana finished the game having shot 34 percent from the field and 16 percent from deep.

The Fever will now wait for an injury update on Boston while preparing to potentially start out the postseason against the defending WNBA champions.

Thursday's loss, combined with the Washington Mystics' victory over the Chicago Sky the same night, will drop the Fever in the WNBA's playoff seeding from No. 5 to No. 6.

Instead of the Atlanta Dream, Fever will now be slated to take on either the Las Vegas Aces or Golden State Valkyries when the postseason tips off this Sunday.

If the Aces claim a Thursday night win over the Phoenix Mercury, Las Vegas will secure the No. 2 seed. The Valkyries could alternatively lock in a first-round matchup against the Fever with a win over the Los Angeles Sparks or an Aces loss.

articles.title: Indiana Fever routed by Lynx in regular season finale as Caitlin Clark posts career-worst performance
articles.summary: Caitlin Clark was held to a career-worst two points on 1-of-12 shooting as the Minnesota Lynx routed the Indiana Fever 86-66 in the finale.
articles.body: Caitlin Clark and the Indiana Fever flamed out in their regular-season finale. Indy stood no chance Thursday night as the top-seeded Minnesota Lynx cruised to an 86-66 beatdown. Fever fans were also watching the Lynx matchup for playoff seeding purposes. With the loss, the Fever fall into a matchup against the defending champion Las Vegas Aces, led by MVP frontrunner A'ja Wilson. With a win, Indiana could have faced the Atlanta Dream. THE CRAIG CARTON SHOW–UNFILTERED, UNAPOLOGETIC AND UNMISSABLE. DOWNLOAD HIS DAILY PODCAST NOW! On Tuesday, Indy faced the Lynx at home and pulled off a statement win, at one point handing Minnesota its biggest deficit of the season. Minnesota extinguished all of Indiana's momentum in the rematch, locking down Caitlin Clark to a career-worst two points on 1-of-12 shooting (1-for-8 at halftime) in 18 minutes of action. The Fever went into the half down 62-32. Minnesota was shorthanded for a second consecutive game with rookie sensation Olivia Miles out again with a calf injury. CAITLIN CLARK RETURNS AFTER FIBA TITLE AS KELSEY MITCHELL SETS WNBA SCORING MARK IN FEVER VICTORY OVER TEMPO The Lynx rested their starters for the bulk of Tuesday's second half. Indiana seemingly followed suit on Thursday after falling behind by 30 in the third quarter, limiting Clark's floor time and seeing Sophie Cunningham held scoreless across 16 minutes. Clark had the opportunity to become the WNBA's first player to reach 900 points and 300 assists in a single season. She entered Thursday's game just 11 points shy of the 900-point mark, but fell short, finishing with two points, three assists, and four rebounds. Indiana's loss was made worse when starting center Aliyah Boston was ruled out with a right lower leg injury. The Fever also lost guard Ty Harris, who was carried off the court. On the bright side for Indy, Kelsey Mitchell broke the single-season three-pointer record, hitting her 135th of the season to pass Rhyne Howard (134). Mitchell led the team with 10 points on the night, though she snapped her streak of consecutive games with 20-plus points, ending her run at 27 games as Indiana finishes the regular season at 28-15. articles.title: Los Lakers defienden su honestidad en la salida de LeBron James y la definen como "amistosa"
articles.standfirst: Rob Pelinka analiza la salida de LeBron James de los Lakers tras ocho temporadas y un anillo de campeón
articles.summary: Rob Pelinka analiza la salida de LeBron James de los Lakers tras ocho temporadas y un anillo de campeón
articles.body: El director general de los Los Angeles Lakers, Rob Pelinka, aseguró que la salida de LeBron James de la franquicia este verano fue "amistosa" y se mostró agradecido por el tiempo que el jugador pasó en el equipo. "Estoy muy agradecido por la relación que tuvimos, que se prolongó hasta este verano, cuando se tomó la decisión de que jugara en otro equipo. Se hizo de manera amistosa, profesional y elegante", aseguró Pelinka en una rueda de prensa. Tras ocho temporadas en Los Ángeles, donde ganó el anillo en 2020, James, de 41 años, firmó este verano para las dos próximas campañas con los Philadelphia 76ers. "Estamos agradecidos por la era de LeBron. Las comunicaciones con él durante este verano se llevaron a cabo de forma diplomática, profesional y honesta", añadió Pelinka. "Vimos todo esto con gratitud, porque ha sido una época increíble para nosotros aquí", insistió el directivo. James anunció el 24 de julio su decisión de fichar por los 76ers después de reconocer que, al final de la temporada pasada, llegó a pensar que se iba a retirar. "Esta es mi última decisión. No lo hago por dinero. No lo hago por mi familia. ¿Por qué sigo jugando a estas alturas? Todavía quiero sacrificarme. Todavía quiero trabajar. Todavía quiero esforzarme. Todavía quiero competir y tener la oportunidad de volver a sentir lo que es ganar", afirmó entonces James.

articles.title: Fever fall to Lynx, drop to No. 6 playoff seed as Ty Harris, Aliyah Boston exit with injuries
articles.summary: Harris left the game in the third quarter, after Indiana had already lost Aliyah Boston to a lower leg injury earlier in the game.
articles.body:
Indiana Fever guard Tyasha Harris exited Thursday's loss to the Minnesota Lynx with what appears to be a severe ankle injury. Minnesota ended up handily beating Indiana, 86-66 , holding the Fever to a season low in points.

After going up for a layup in the third quarter of Thursday's game, Harris went down, clutching her left ankle and clearly in a lot of pain. She had to be carried off the court by staff, who took her back into the locker room.

The Fever officially ruled her out shortly afterward with a left ankle injury.

Earlier in the game, Indiana had lost Aliyah Boston to a right lower leg injury, with the star center checking out in the second quarter. Boston did not start in the second half, with the team ruling Boston out for the rest of the game during the third quarter. After the game, head coach Stephanie White didn't have an update on Harris , but said Boston experienced a flare-up of the lower leg injury she had earlier this season.

The game, which marked the regular-season finale for both teams, only held seeding significance for Indiana. A win would've made them the No. 5 seed and sent them to Atlanta to play the Dream. Instead, they secured the No. 6 spot. Both teams clinched their playoff spots last month, with Minnesota securing the No. 1 overall seed on Tuesday.

A lack of urgency was a little obvious in the matchup, especially from the Fever, who saw an uncharacteristically low-scoring game. The Fever scored just nine points in the third quarter, and star guard Caitlin Clark had an off night, scoring just two points off 1-of-12 shooting from the floor.

Minnesota, meanwhile, had a hot 62-point first half before letting its starters take a break on the bench. Kayla McBride ended with 22 points for the Lynx, and Natasha Howard chipped in 21 points; Fever guard Kelsey Mitchell , who scored 10 points, was the only other player on either team to break double digits.

articles.title: Aces overwhelm Mercury for momentum heading into playoff rematch
articles.summary: PHOENIX—Closing out the year with one rematch from last year’s playoff, the Las Vegas Aces now find themselves preparing for battle against another formerly...
articles.body:
PHOENIX—Closing out the year with one rematch from last year's playoff, the Las Vegas Aces now find themselves preparing for battle against another formerly vanquished foe.

On Thursday, the Aces closed out the regular season with a bang, with A'ja Wilson and Chelsea Gray hitting double-doubles in a 100-82 victory over the Phoenix Mercury .

The win puts the Aces at seven straight to end the year, pushing them into the playoffs with serious momentum by their side once again.

Wilson put an exclamation point on her case for her fifth MVP award, securing 34 points and 10 rebounds as well as four assists and a steal. The performance guarantees that Wilson secures over 26 points per game for the second time in her career, the only player in WNBA history to reach that mark even once. Gray would also end the regular season with a strong effort, putting up 12 points while adding ten assists and five steals to continue providing value on both ends of the court.

Even Jackie Young , despite having a cold scoring night with only five points, made her presence felt elsewhere with a game-high 11 assists, seven rebounds and three steals.

However, Young's struggles to generate points made the other developments of the game so much more important for the Aces.

Stephanie Talbot , who has spent the season trying to find her fit in Las Vegas , appears to have turned the corner and is getting hot at the right time. The Aussie wing has returned from the World Cup with a vengeance, putting up 14 points, four rebounds and two steals.

"We've had 44 games to kind of work on our chemistry and figure each other out and hopefully it's all coming together at the right time," said Talbot. "Coming into playoffs, everyone's feeling good, so it's exciting."

Meanwhile, Jewell Loyd appears to have flipped a switch at the right time, providing microwave scoring with 25 points in as many minutes. This includes a game-high five three-point shots, which was more than the rest of the Aces put together.

"I think we've been stacking games together," said Loyd about the Aces' depth coming through at the right time. "Whether it's Steph coming in, Mai [Yamamoto], Cheyenne [Parker-Tyus], I think that's the job is to try to find energy on both sides of the floor.

We want to use this momentum to hopefully push us to the end and, when we play together, remember when we're excited for each other. I think that's how we play. It's just better basketball that way."

It was an important game for solutions to be found, as the Aces find themselves looking at a stern test for the first round of the WNBA playoffs.

By virtue of the Minnesota Lynx blowing out the Indiana Fever and the Golden State Valkyries roaring back against the Los Angeles Sparks to secure the second seed, the Aces get a semifinals rematch against the Fever to kickstart the journey for their fourth title in five years. Making the matchup all the more compelling is the added element of Caitlin Clark , who missed last year's playoffs due to injury. Needless to say, the Aces' path towards cementing themselves as a dynasty will not be easy.

"Obviously, they have a high-powered offense, so that's job number one is slowing them up a little bit. Easier said than done," said Aces head coach Becky Hammon about the Fever. "It's going to be a tall task for us but, coming in, we know that defense is a game changer and we're going to need a lot of it against them."

The series, as well as the WNBA playoffs, tip off on Sunday. Game One will take place at Michelob ULTRA Arena at a time to be determined.

articles.title: ‘Didn’t Do That for Caitlin (Clark),’ ‘Fire This Fool’ — Outrage Erupts As Stephanie White Reps Kelsey Mitchell Shirt at Fever’s Regular-Season Finale
articles.summary: Nothing went Caitlin Clark’s way during the Indiana Fever’s regular-season finale against the top-seeded Minnesota Lynx on Thursday. The three-time WNBA All-...
articles.body:
Nothing went Caitlin Clark 's way during the Indiana Fever 's regular-season finale against the top-seeded Minnesota Lynx on Thursday. The three-time WNBA All-Star recorded a career-low 2 points on woefully inefficient 1-for-12 shooting in the 86-66 blowout loss.

Clark didn't seem to get much support from the sideline either, as coach Stephanie White appeared in a Kelsey Mitchell Slam shirt. Clark's fanbase was furious over the lack of similar support from coach White for the WNBA superstar.

Caitlin Clark Fans Furious Over Stephanie White Wearing Kelsey Mitchell Shirt

Clark had the chance to add another record to her name. She could have become the first point guard in WNBA history to post 900 points in a single season. She was only 11 points shy. Instead, she fizzled out with her lowest-scoring game ever.

Mitchell, on the other hand, added another piece of history to her résumé. With two made 3-pointers on 6 attempts, she broke the WNBA single-season record with 135 triples.

Mitchell has been a reliable scorer throughout the 2026 season, posting a team-high 24.7 points per game. However, the four-time WNBA All-Star saw her historic 27-game 20-point streak end as she scored only 10 points against the Lynx in the final outing of the season.

Still, White in a Mitchell shirt didn't sit well with Clark supporters, who didn't hold back from digging into the Fever coach with pointed jabs.

"Stephanie White and the coaching staff wearing Kelsey Mitchell Slam shirts but didn't do that for Caitlin's Slam Kicks cover for her highly anticipated Nike shoes. Very on brand for this staff," one fan wrote .

"Stephanie White is doing everything she can to hype KM for MVP over Caitlin Clark, when Caitlin has broken so many records…KM isn't [expletive] without Caitlin Clark assisting her on her shots," another added .

"Stephanie White always reppin her fav!" one Clark loyalist asserted , arguing that White frequently shows more support for Mitchell than Clark.

Amid Clark and Mitchell's lackluster production, the Fever were run out of the building by the Lynx's relentless offense. They suffered their biggest defeat of the season.

Putting Indiana's plight in context, one X user wrote , "And look how the game is going."

"Nope NEVER! Fire this fool," another X user wrote .

Meanwhile, a few supporters believed the shirt pointed to a bigger divide within the Fever, with one asserting , "The whole coaching staff is wearing a KM shirt. They're showing they're united and F CC. I have never seen something so aggressive from a staff."

The criticism did not stop there, as a fan bluntly declared , "I legitimately despise Steph White. She is the worst thing to ever happen to the Fever. She's a bad coach and a worse human being."

While the Mitchell Slam shirt became a talking point, the bigger story is that the Lynx steamrolled the Fever with a 20-point win, sapping their momentum right before the playoffs.

The loss dropped Indiana to the No. 6 seed at 28-16. The Fever will now face the No. 3-seeded Las Vegas Aces in the first round, with the series set to begin Sunday.

The only relief for the Fever might be the fact that they won the regular-season series against Las Vegas 2-1, including both road matchups.

Still, Clark will have to put the disappointing regular-season finale behind her quickly. The Fever will need Clark at her best to stand a chance against the defending WNBA champions in Round 1 of the 2026 playoffs.

articles.title: Tyler Herro Trade Idea To Fix 1 Contender's Biggest Flaw
articles.summary: The Detroit Pistons' offseason moves were all about collecting shooters to space the floor, but what if adding Isaiah Joe, John Collins, Gary Harris and Taurean Prince doesn't solve the team's half-court scoring issues?
articles.body:
The Detroit Pistons' offseason moves were all about collecting shooters to space the floor, but what if adding Isaiah Joe, John Collins, Gary Harris and Taurean Prince doesn't solve the team's half-court scoring issues?

Anyone who watched postseason defenses sell out to stop Cade Cunningham knows the Pistons need playmakers at least as badly as they need shooters. Daniss Jenkins was hugely helpful last season, but he remains the only proven shot-creator behind Detroit's MVP candidate.

Let's cook up a deal to get the Pistons help at the point of attack in All-Star guard Tyler Herro.

Milwaukee Bucks Acquire: Ron Holland, Duncan Robinson, 2027 unprotected first-round pick

Herro has averaged at least 20.0 points per game in each of the last five seasons, but it's not just his scoring volume that makes him a fit with the Pistons. It's how he goes about getting his numbers.

In every season of his career, Herro has scored more than half of his two-point baskets without the benefit of a teammate assist. Last year, Cunningham, Jenkins and the departed Caris LeVert were the only players ranking among Detroit's top 10 in minutes who joined Herro in making most of their twos without an assist.

That kind of self-sufficient bucket-getting skill is exactly what the Pistons need to take the pressure off of Cunningham while also maximizing the value of their setup-dependent shooters.

It also doesn't hurt Detroit's long-term roster plans that Holland is one of the outgoing pieces. If the Pistons are committed to Ausar Thompson, the "good wing who can't shoot" quota is already met. Everyone loves the hustle and defensive intensity both Thompson and Holland provide, but playing (and paying) both just never made sense.

Herro is on an expiring $33 million salary, which limits the Pistons' exposure if this doesn't work out. All of the shooting acquired in free agency should easily offset the loss of Robinson.

Rebuilding in the first year of its post-Giannis Antetokounmpo era, Milwaukee should be in the business of hoarding as many future first-rounders as possible. It lands one here in exchange for Herro.

The Bucks might put some extra hometown value on the Wisconsin native, but they also need to be wary of committing to him on a new contract. Turning him into Holland and Robinson makes more financial sense for a couple of reasons.

Holland is entering his third year and could either be extended next summer or retained using the rapidly rising power of restricted free agency in 2028. Robinson has one more year on his deal after this one, but his $15.2 million for 2027-28 is non-guaranteed.

In Holland, the Bucks get a cost-controlled prospect whose defensive intensity and athleticism should pair well with 2025-26 breakout guard Ryan Rollins and recent No. 10 pick Brayden Burries. Those two can run the offense while Holland does the dirty work. Milwaukee will certainly hope the No. 5 pick in the 2024 draft adds some perimeter accuracy to his game, but his current flaws matter less here than they would in Detroit.

articles.title: 10 NBA Players With the Most to Lose at Training Camp
articles.summary: The NBA reopening its doors is generally a joyful occasion. For a handful of players, though, training camp is also a stressful affair.
articles.body:
The NBA reopening its doors is generally a joyful occasion. For a handful of players, though, training camp is also a stressful affair.

Some people are fighting for a spot on their team. Others are trying to save their careers. Plenty of players are vying for the right to fend off someone—if not multiple someones—coming for their minutes.

When spotlighting who has the most on the line, we will be on the lookout for position battles, second acts and NBA livelihood. We'll stick to only the most notable situations.

Players under guaranteed contracts who might still get bounced from their roster. Incumbent starters who could get displaced from the opening five. Rotation mainstays facing role reductions. Familiar faces trying to restart once-promising careers. These all take precedence over your typical training-camp invitee trying to earn an opening-night roster spot.

The Stakes: A guaranteed spot in the rotation

Somebody from the Washington Wizards' perimeter jumble will find themselves displaced amid the body-count glut and elevated expectations . By process of elimination, Bub Carrington lands near the front of the chopping-block line.

Trae Young, AJ Dybantsa and Kyshawn George are all going to receive their fair share of on-ball reps. For all of Washington's depth, it's light on long-range flamethrowers. That gives Tre Johnson a level of security, as does the fact that he was drafted at No. 6 barely a year ago.

Bilal Coulibaly's offensive limitations could let him slip by the wayside, but the Wizards need an ace defensive option unless they envision Dybantsa becoming that guy. Even if they do, he'll need time to become that guy. Coulibaly will remain a necessity at least to start the year.

This leaves Carrington to compete for minutes with Will Riley, Justin Champagnie and Khris Middleton. That internal jockeying is only complicated by Washington's frontcourt.

Having Anthony Davis, Alex Sarr and Deandre Ayton all on the roster implies a commitment to dual-big units. That inherently limits how many four-guard/wing lineups the Wizards deploy. So where Carrington's positional size and on-ball poise once guaranteed him a prominent spot in the rotation, it doesn't anymore.

The Stakes: Remaining a part of the frontcourt plans.

Somebody from the Utah Jazz's regular rotation is getting the boot this season. Kyle Filipowski joins Isaiah Collier and Brice Sensabaugh in the "How important are these guys to a team trying to win?" pressure cooker.

Collier is safest. Utah doesn't have much playmaking behind Keyonte George and Darryn Peterson, both of whom could start. Brice Sensabaugh could get buried behind veteran arrivals Josh Okogie and Josh Green, but anyone shooting 38 percent from deep for their career while slinging 'em at a rate of nearly nine per 36 minutes has an easier time overcoming defensive (and ball-stopping) challenges.

Jaren Jackson Jr. and Lauri Markkanen are going to cannibalize minutes at the 4. The competition at center isn't overwhelming, but the Jazz have gotten flamed whenever Filipowski plays the 5. Lineups with Jusuf Nurkić, Jaxson Hayes or Jackson in the middle all profile as better options.

Please don't even think about head coach Will Hardy rolling Filipowski out as a de facto 3. Utah's jumbo-sized concoctions have their limits. This is one of them. Filipowski hasn't shot nearly well or frequently enough from distance to indulge the defensive concessions ingrained into that experiment.

Where does that leave him? It's a great question. And it may already have an answer. For Filipowski's sake, he better hope he still has time to flip it.

The Stakes: A spot in the starting lineup...if not the rotation at all.

Jalen Green's place in the Phoenix Suns' pecking order is more tenuous than it should be for a team's second-highest-paid player. What he theoretically does best isn't necessarily duplicative, but between last year's hamstring issues and a rickety track record, his fit remains the subject of skepticism.

Can his athleticism lead to more pressure at the rim and better efficiency once he gets there ? Can he consistently be more than a league-average shooter on spot-up jumpers? If he has the ball in his hands, can he play-make effectively enough to lighten Devin Booker's workload?

History doesn't portend optimistic answers to these questions. Green needs to change that, because pay grade and potential aren't enough to promise him anything.

Phoenix has Collin Gillespie, Jordan Goodwin and Luke Kennard to gobble up backcourt minutes alongside Booker. The price paid for Miles Bridges is nothing if proof that the Suns plan to feature him when Booker's catching a breather. The same presumably goes for Dillon Brooks following his extension.

If Green isn't checking enough of the complementary boxes or living up to his perceived strengths, his status as a starter isn't the only thing at stake. A general spot in the rotation will be, too.

The Stakes: His place in the backcourt pecking order—and Portland's future.

Little about how the Portland Trail Blazers have operated over the past few seasons suggests they're confident in Scoot Henderson's availability or overall ability. The flashes he showed last year when healthy, particularly as a starter, weren't enough to stop them from continuing that trend this summer.

Ja Morant's ball dominance, questionable shooting and suspect defense are now entering the mix. Damian Lillard is returning from an Achilles injury. Shaedon Sharpe's torn right meniscus buys flexibility, but it's temporary. Portland also has Deni Avdija's star turn and Jrue Holiday on the roster.

Deploying Holiday like a wing lets the Blazers tap into three-guard structures pretty easily. Lillard has plenty of experience playing off the rock as well. But he and Morant have generally spent more than 40 percent of their offensive possessions as on-ball creators. Avdija, meanwhile, is coming off a 99th-percentile season of on-ball volume.

While everyone is under pressure to adapt, Henderson is the least established. His on-ball percentage will need to drop. His volume and efficiency out of spot-ups, hand-offs and screens will have to climb. His defense will have to be good enough to log heavy minutes alongside at least one of Lillard and Morant.

Failing to work within Portland's roster framework doesn't just stand to cost Henderson minutes. Entering a contract year, his ability to reorient his game could determine what jersey he's wearing past the Feb. 11 trade deadline.

The Stakes: His spot in the starting lineup.

If you are not surprised by this inclusion, well, you should be. Despite a checkered health bill over the past two years and scoring lines that make the points-per-game's crowd eyes bleed, Herb Jones has proven time and time again that he helps drive some of the New Orleans Pelicans' most effective lineups.

Naturally, the soon-to-be 28-year-old will continue to start entering next season, just as he has for 97 percent of his career games.

Shamit Dua of In The N.O. dropped a small-but-significant truth bomb on Twitter, writing: "I think [the Pelicans] want to start [Jeremiah] Fears. Would not be surprised to see Fears, Dejounte [Murray], Trey [Murphy III], Zion [Williamson and Yves] Missi."

Starting a sophomore not known for his stopping power over a potential All-Defense candidate isn't head coach Jamahl Mosley's style. But perhaps he's turning over a new, offense-first leap. Or maybe this is a mandate from up top.

Either way, it appears Jones will have to scrap and claw to retain his starting role.

The Stakes: Backup power forward minutes.

Nikola Jović finished last season outside the Miami Heat's rotation. As he kicks off a four-year, $62.4 million extension that's at risk of aging into one of the NBA's worst deals, the path back into head coach Erik Spoelstra's good graces isn't going to be easy.

Healthy Giannis Antetokounmpo eats up 30-36 minutes of the power forward rotation. That doesn't leave much wiggle room for his primary backup.

For the record, Jović isn't guaranteed to be the primary backup. Even if the Heat view Bobby Portis as their second-string 5, he'll still see minutes at the 4 if Nick Richards makes the roster. Failing that, the Heat have no qualms about sliding Andrew Wiggins or Simone Fontecchio to power forward.

Jović's utility rises if Miami can buy time with him at the 3 or the 5. It can't. His one-position limitations put him at a disadvantage no matter what. They do him even more harm with Giannis in town.

Without a top-notch training camp, Jović may begin this year where he finished last season: on the outside looking in at everything Miami is trying to do.

The Stakes: The final starting-lineup spot, but also more.

Four of the Los Angeles Lakers' five starters are etched in stone: Luka Dončić, Austin Reaves, Walker Kessler and Quentin Grimes. For a hot minute, it looked like Jake LaRavia would comfortably round it out.

Then, the Lakers signed Sandro Mamukelashvili. And Ziaire Williams. And Matisse Thybulle. Then the Adou Thiero hype train continued rolling along.

Now, you can't help but wonder whether LaRavia is fighting for more than a chance to start. Or whether he's even an option to start.

Based on what the Lakers need most, Williams is the best fit to cherry-top the opening five. Wing minutes will be available coming off the bench, but they'll be harder to pin down if head coach JJ Redick is willing to play Mamu at the 4 and Thiero is getting regular burn.

On the bright side, LaRavia's path to assurance is clear: take more than 4.2 threes per 36 minutes , make more than 32.1 percent of them and defend at a higher level than last season. Whether he can satisfy enough of this checklist is a separate matter—one that'll determine not just when he plays, but how much.

Terrence Shannon Jr., Minnesota Timberwolves

The Stakes: Winning the seventh- or eighth-man role.

Terrence Shannon Jr. wrapped up an injury-riddled sophomore campaign by once again showing signs of life in the playoffs. The pressure he put on defenses going downhill left head coach Chris Finch lamenting how he'd been used when healthy.

"We've learned, with [Shannon], he's gotta have the ball in his hands ," Finch explained. "Silly me, we played him out of the corner most of the season, but he's way better with the ball in his hands at the top of the floor."

This assessment now comes across as an indictment.

Putting the rock in TSJ's hands is no longer as feasible with Anthony Edwards, LaMelo Ball, Ayo Dosunmu and Jonathan Kuminga ahead of him in the pecking order. With the Minnesota Timberwolves' top-six—if not top-seven (Joan Beringer)—spots in the rotation locked up, Shannon needs to do more of the accessory work.

That doesn't mean he has to live in the corner. It does mean he needs to hit his threes, make quicker decisions with the ball, consistently defend and compete for rebounds. If TSJ isn't able to deliver on the first two items, Jaylen Clark overtaking him in the hierarchy will be the least of his worries. In that scenario, he could find himself fending off Cody Williams.

The Stakes: Head coach Ime Udoka's affection.

Reed Sheppard more than tripled his total court time from his rookie to sophomore season. All it took was Fred VanVleet missing the entire year and the Houston Rockets resisting the urge to add a veteran ball-handler better than Aaron Holiday.

Dynamics have shifted entering Sheppard's third season. VanVleet is back. We can't discount the Rockets signing Marcus Smart. Though his knack for defending up allows him to replace both Josh Okogie and the idea of Dorian Finney-Smith, Houston is still adding two guards it didn't have last year to its rotation.

Sheppard's shooting gives him some measure of job security. Nobody on the Rockets came close to making as many threes last year. He was one of just 10 players leaguewide to make 39 percent or more of his triples on more than 500 total attempts.

Still, Sheppard hasn't flashed as much on-ball escapism as initially hoped. Despite ratcheting up his playing time last year, Udoka didn't entrust him with a ton of featured responsibility. Sheppard ranked in the 35th percentile in on-ball possessions used.

Roster construction explains some of the usage, including times when the 22-year-old is treated like the fourth or fifth option in crunch-time situations . Alperen Şengün, Amen Thompson and Kevin Durant all usurp him in the pecking order.

None of which lowers the stakes for Sheppard. His margin for error shrinks with both VanVleet and Smart around him. The Rockets don't seem poised to expand his usage even if he's raining haymakers and holding his own on defense. Unless he becomes undeniable, Sheppard's chance at a star or fringe-star turn in Houston seems to be running out of steam.

The Stakes: Retaining his status as the third big.

Don't look now, but the Oklahoma City Thunder have a quadrillion centers on the roster.

OK, actually, it's five. But that's still one-third of a 15-man roster.

Chet Holmgren and Isaiah Hartenstein have nothing to worry about. Jaylin Williams is a different story.

Thomas Sorber, selected 15th overall in 2025, is set to make his NBA debut after missing last year with a torn right ACL. The Thunder also just drafted Aday Mara at No. 15 . While his summer league performances were iffy, he tore it up during FIBA action with Spain.

Getting both rookie bigs minutes is a must, which puts Williams' court time in jeopardy. This wouldn't have been the case in years past. OKC has always excelled at juggling player development and relevance. Head coach Mark Daigneault would have sprinkled in reps during blowouts, or on nights in which he felt comfortable taking it easy on Holmgren or Hartenstein.

The Thunder's stakes are different now—higher overall and more difficult to navigate. They faced their first second-apron crunch over the offseason. It cost them Lu Dort, Aaron Wiggins and Isaiah Joe. The depth that has traditionally bought them the flexibility necessary to develop their mystery boxes is now the mystery boxes themselves.

Between that and what could be stiffer night-to-night competition in the new lottery era, more of OKC's experimental reps have to come when it matters. Williams better watch his six. The Thunder's financial situation leaves them little choice other than to try finding and developing his and even Hartenstein's eventual replacement.

Dan Favale is a National NBA Writer for Bleacher Report. Follow him on Bluesky ( @danfavale ), and subscribe to the Hardwood Knocks podcast, co-hosted by Bleacher Report's Grant Hughes .

articles.title: Valanciunas reclama su rol de estrella de la Euroliga y Obradovic es aclamado en su regreso a Atenas
articles.standfirst: El pívot del Zalgiris (13+8) fue de los más destacados en una primera noche con protagonismo del mítico entrenador, Lessort, Francisco, Yabusele, Mills, Crowder...
articles.summary: El pívot del Zalgiris (13+8) fue de los más destacados en una primera noche con protagonismo del mítico entrenador, Lessort, Francisco, Yabusele, Mills, Crowder...
articles.body: La primera tarde-noche de Euroliga esta temporada trajo el regreso a la competición de Jonas Valanciunas. El pívot lituano no la disputaba desde 2011, cuando militaba en el Lietuvos Rytas. Ahora ha vuelto después de 14 temporadas en la NBA y, en su primer partido, ya demostró que puede ser un factor diferencial. Le sufrió Ibon Navarro, que se estrenaba con el Estrella Roja en competición europea. En la victoria en Belgrado por 77-83, el coloso lituano de 34 años y 2,11 metros terminó con 13 puntos (6/9 en tiros de campo), ocho rebotes, tres tapones y 24 de valoración. Y eso, pudiendo estar en pista menos de 22 minutos. Un golpe en la nariz de Jordan Nwora le hizo irse al banquillo sangrando al comienzo del segundo cuarto y en el último también tuvo que ser atendido. Su mejor socio fue Azuolas Tubelis, que en el estreno confirmó las buenas vibraciones que transmitió la temporada pasada. Hizo 10 puntos, 12 rebotes y 23 de valoración. El mejor en las filas serbias fue Chris Jones, ex del Valencia Basket y el Hapoel Tel Aviv. Anotó 15 puntos y repartió ocho asistencias. La Euroliga también vio el regreso de Zeljko Obradovic a Atenas. Como en los viejos tiempos, fue ovacionado por los aficionados del Panathinaikos al ritmo de 'El Porompompero', de Manolo Escobar. El entrenador más laureado de Europa, con nueve entorchados, cinco de ellos con el club ateniense, condujo a su equipo a un cómodo triunfo sobre el París Basketball por 91-72. En el primer cuarto ya mandaba por 31-17. La mejor actuación la firmó Mathias Lessort, que ya brilló con Obradovic en el Partizan. El pívot francés se fue a 15 puntos (11/12 en tiros libres) y nueve rebotes para 28 de valoración en 21:53 minutos en pista. Había expectación por ver a los fichajes del gigante griego. Sylvain Francisco hizo 18 puntos y cuatro asistencias, el exmadridista Guerschon Yabusele sumó 13 tantos y cinco capturas y Brancou Badio, ex del Valencia Basket, se quedó en cuatro puntos. Juancho Hernangómez jugó algo más de 20 minutos para terminar con cinco puntos, seis rebotes, una asistencias y dos recuperaciones. A sus 38 años, Patty Mills se estrenó en la Euroliga con el ASVEL y dejó buenas sensaciones. El base australiano fue uno de los mejores de su equipo con 15 puntos y tres asistencias. Jae Crowder, otro con mucha experiencia NBA, fue el más destacado con 19 puntos, cuatro rebotes, cuatro asistencias y 25 de valoración. Los galos vencieron al Maccabi Tel Aviv por 84-74 sumando el primer triunfo de la era Tony Parker en el banquillo. Al Hapoel Tel Aviv, mientras, no le bastó con la actuación de Dan Oturu para conseguir derrotar al Bayern Múnich, que se llevó el triunfo por 84-86. El pívot firmó 20 puntos, 12 rebotes y 32 de valoración. A los alemanes, en el estreno de Anton Gavel en el banquillo, les comandó Andreas Obst con 19 puntos (3/6 en triples).

articles.title: El Barça también pierde a Nebo y el juego interior queda muy tocado
articles.standfirst: Con una lesión en el sóleo de la pierna derecha, se suma a Evbuomwan y Makoundou en la enfermería: Balcerowski, único pívot puro
articles.summary: Con una lesión en el sóleo de la pierna derecha, se suma a Evbuomwan y Makoundou en la enfermería: Balcerowski, único pívot puro
articles.body: Los problemas físicos acosan al Barcelona en este inicio de temporada y se están cebando especialmente en el juego interior. El último en caer ha sido Josh Nebo, al que se le detectó una lesión en el sóleo de la pierna derecha producida en el entrenamiento de este miércoles. El tiempo de recuperación estimado por los servicios médicos del conjunto azulgranas es de entre dos y tres semanas. Este jueves ya fue baja en la victoria sobre el Anadolu Efes en el estreno de la Euroliga. Nebo se suma a otros dos de los recién llegados, que también están en la enfermería. Tosan Evbuomwan sufrió una subluxación del hombro izquierdo durante un partido de las Ventanas FIBA con Gran Bretaña y, aunque su evolución es positiva, debe seguir haciendo trabajo de readaptación durante las próximas semanas. Y a Yoan Makoundou le resta aproximadamente un mes para estar recuperado de su lesión por una agudización de una tendinopatía rotuliana en la rodilla izquierda. El 11 de septiembre, el equipo azulgrana informó que se sometería a un tratamiento conservador y que estaría unas seis semanas de baja. Con esa situación, el juego interior del Barcelona queda maltrecho, pues Olek Balcerowski es el único pívot puro. Ante el Efes, el entrenador Aleksander Sekulic encontró recursos como la polivalencia de Olivier Nkamhoua y jugar con quintetos pequeños. Será la misma receta para el estreno de este sábado en la Liga Endesa ante el recién ascendido Leyma Coruña y para la primera doble jornada de Euroliga de la próxima semana, con visitas al Dubai Basketball de Xavi Pascual y al Besiktas.

articles.title: Arranca la segunda edición de la Liga U, donde crecen las estrellas del futuro
articles.standfirst: Este viernes se alza el telón de la competición U22 con las mejores canteras de la ACB y el favoritismo del Barcelona y el Real Madrid, que defiende título
articles.summary: Este viernes se alza el telón de la competición U22 con las mejores canteras de la ACB y el favoritismo del Barcelona y el Real Madrid, que defiende título
articles.body: La segunda edición de la Liga U levanta el telón este viernes. El proyecto nacido para dar continuidad al talento joven de los clubes ACB e impulsada también por la Federación Española y el CSD promete ir a más en este segundo año. Las estrellas del futuro, jugadores U22, tendrán un escenario exigente antes del salto profesional. No hay un mejor escaparate para ellos. El partido inaugural enfrentará al Burgos Grupo de Santiago y al Barça Atlètic, dos equipos que disputaron la Final a 6. Ambos estarán en el Grupo A junto al Real Madrid, vigente campeón, Casademont Zaragoza, Fundación CB Canarias, Valencia Basket y Bàsquet Girona. En el B competirán Kids&Us Manresa, Joventut, Amara Lleida, Euskaltax Bilbao Basket, UCAM Murcia Juver, Unicaja Alhaurín de la Torre y Obradoiro. La primera fase llegará hasta el 19 de diciembre y tendrá 14 jornadas, con los equipos divididos en esos dos grupos y partidos a doble vuelta. Después llegará un play-out y los cruces decidirán qué equipos jugarán la segunda fase en el Grupo A y cuáles lo harán en el B. La segunda fase comenzará el 4 de enero y se extenderá hasta el 17 de abril. Después llegará la Final Six, del 13 al 16 de mayo, que decidirá al campeón. Los grandes, favoritos El Real Madrid afronta la defensa del título después de derrotar al Barcelona la temporada pasada en la final. Dado el dominio y el historial reciente de las canteras de los dos grandes del baloncesto español, volverán a partir como grandes favoritos. Pero que no se confíen. En la primera edición también se intuía un paseo de blancos y culés y se dejaron triunfos por el camino. Las promesas del baloncesto español llegan con hambre.

articles.title: Cooper Flagg's NBA Rookie Debut Patch Autograph sells for $8.04M at auction, becomes third-most expensive NBA card ever
articles.summary: One of the most anticipated auctions in collecting history ended early Friday morning, with Cooper Flagg’s NBA Rookie Debut Patch Auto selling for $8.04 mill...
articles.body:
One of the most anticipated auctions in collecting history ended early Friday morning, with Cooper Flagg's NBA Rookie Debut Patch Auto selling for $8.04 million, making it one of the most expensive sports cards ever sold.

The card, auctioned on the Fanatics Collect platform, is now the third-most expensive NBA card ever, trailing only two dual logomen (Kobe Bryant-Michael Jordan and Jordan-LeBron James) which each sold last year for eight figures. The Flagg RDPA — graded a perfect PSA 10 for both the card and autograph — now also represents his highest card sale ever, with the previous record standing at $366K.

After his Rookie of the Year campaign , the one-of-one Flagg became one of the biggest chase cards ever , sparking a frenzy over the summer as Topps released its Topps Chrome Basketball Update set. The Mavericks offered an impressive bounty for the card, including signed memorabilia, VIP experiences and 32 years of lower-level season tickets.

Ultimately, the card's redemption was pulled in an online break by Rhody Breakers last month and the winner — identified as South Carolina man Jason Williams — opted to consign the life-changing card to Fanatics rather than accepting the Mavericks' bounty or using the Alt platform, which held a pre-auction that guaranteed a sale of at least $3.8M. Ken Goldin also offered a $1.5M cash advance if the card were to be consigned to his auction house.

In addition to Flagg's card, similar RDPA's for Spurs rookie Dylan Harper and Hornets rookie Kon Knueppel also sold early Friday morning in the same auction. Harper's card sold for $2.88M and Knueppel's for $2.34M. The three RDPA's were the only cards in the premier auction to sell for more than $1M and now represent the three highest sales for such cards across any sport.

Topps introduced Rookie Debut Patch Autograph cards in its MLB product in 2023, but they did not become a mainstream craze until the following year, when Paul Skenes' version led to a hunt similar to Flagg's. Skenes' RDPA was eventually pulled by a young collector and sold to Dick's Sporting Goods for $1.11M and put on display in a Pittsburgh-area store.

articles.title: Cooper Flagg's NBA Rookie Debut Patch Card Sells for $8M in Historic Auction
articles.summary: Dallas Mavericks superstar Cooper Flagg's one-of-one Topps Chrome Update  rookie debut patch autograph card has sold for more than $8 million after 83 bids in a Fanatics Collect auction that closed early Friday morning.
articles.body:
Dallas Mavericks superstar Cooper Flagg's one-of-one Topps Chrome Update rookie debut patch autograph card has sold for more than $8 million after 83 bids in a Fanatics Collect auction that closed early Friday morning.

The sale smashed the record for the sale of any Flagg card by more than $7 million, and it marked the third-most expensive NBA card sale in history.

The record price for an NBA card is $12,932,000 for a 2007-08 Upper Deck Exquisite Collection Dual Logoman signed by Michael Jordan and Kobe Bryant. The second-most expensive NBA card ever sold is a one-of-one Michael Jordan and LeBron James 2006-07 Upper Deck Exquisite dual NBA Logoman patch autograph that cleared $10 million in a private sale.

According to The Athletic , Friday's sale makes Flagg's card the fifth-most expensive sale of any trading card in history, topping a $7.25 million sale of the famed Honus Wagner 1909 Sweet Caporal T206 in 2022.

Flagg signed the card during this year's Fanatics Fest in July. The card then went out into the world for one lucky fan to find in a pack.

That fan was Jason Williams of South Carolina, per ESPN .

Williams " acquired the card after spending $515 to purchase a spot on the stream of RhodyBreakers, a division of the Baseball Cards of Rhode Island retail shop that opens boxes of trading cards on a livestream for clients," according to ESPN.

"They slid that card over and I just slid to the floor crying," Williams told ESPN. "... It took me about five seconds to realize what I was looking at on that screen."

Williams eventually consigned the card to Fanatics Collect later in August.

Flagg was one of the most hyped draft prospects in recent memory after starring at Duke during the 2024-25 season, when he earned consensus national player of the year honors. The Mavs selected him first overall in the 2025 NBA draft.

The 19-year-old is easily meeting the hype so far, averaging 21.0 points on 46.8 percent shooting, 6.7 rebounds, 4.5 assists and 1.2 steals per game in his Rookie of the Year campaign.

Given his trajectory, it's no surprise the one-on-one card, which features Flagg's rookie debut patch from his Mavs jersey at his first-ever game, sell for such a staggering figure.

Flagg made his debut on Oct. 22, 2025 vs. the San Antonio Spurs. He finished with 10 points and 10 rebounds in a 125-92 loss.

The ex-Duke star enjoyed some fantastic games over his rookie season, including a career-high 51-point outing against the Orlando Magic on April 3.

He followed that up with a near 45-point triple double (nine assists, eight rebounds) in a 134-128 win over the Los Angeles Lakers.

His late-season surge should foreshadow a fantastic sophomore season and an excellent career. In the meantime, one fan clearly believes in his potential and is now in possession of a valuable one-of-one card.

articles.title: A Hidden Struggle: Stephen Curry Makes Surprising Revelation About an Issue He Faced Since His Early NBA Days
articles.summary: Stephen Curry has spent his career being underestimated in one specific way, even his own front office didn't fully grasp it until recently.
articles.body: Stephen Curry has spent his career being underestimated in one specific way, even his own front office didn't fully grasp it until recently. Behind the four championships and the shooting motion nobody's figured out how to stop, there was a detail about how he actually processes the game that stayed mostly unknown.Curry recently talked about it publicly for the first time, and it changes how those title runs look in hindsight. It started with a phone call from his coaching staff.Stephen Curry opens up about the eye condition that shaped his best yearsStephen Curry says a rare condition called keratoconus quietly altered how he saw the court during Golden State's title years, and for a while he had no idea anything was wrong. Diagnosed in 2018, the irregular shape of his cornea left him seeing blurred, distorted images for stretches without a clear explanation. "I didn't know I was really dealing with crazy blurred vision," Curry told PEOPLE, describing how he simply built his game around a problem he couldn't yet name.The discovery came almost by accident. Then-Warriors general manager Bob Myers noticed him squinting during a road broadcast and pushed him to get his eyes checked, a nudge that led straight to the diagnosis. Doctors explained the condition was progressive and could worsen without care, which sent him toward contact lenses he found tough to adjust to at first. These days he gets checked every six months and tells others to do the same, joking that his memoir might be titled "The Whole Time I Couldn't See." Between 2015 and 2022, four championships came anyway.Curry's contract call and shooting numbers still headline Warriors talkWhile that revelation reframes part of his legacy, Curry is also at the center of a very present decision. The 38-year-old is eligible for a two-year, $136.7 million extension, and Golden State has left the timeline entirely up to him. He isn't treating it like a distraction, insisting the process won't change how hard he plays either way and that he'll sign only once he's weighed every angle himself.Former coach PJ Carlesimo isn't ready to call this the end of Golden State's window, either. "Steph hasn't lost anything," Carlesimo said, pointing to a roster that still has bite when everyone is healthy. He argued a fully fit trio of Curry, Draymond Green and Jimmy Butler still gives the Warriors a real shot, brushing off the idea that time has already run out.Even now, comparisons keep popping up that show why his standard is still the one everyone measures against. articles.title: WNBA Playoff Bracket Predictions for Every 2026 Series
articles.summary: The 2026 WNBA playoff bracket is set, and this year's pool feels more wide open than it's been in years.
articles.body:
The 2026 WNBA playoff bracket is set, and this year's pool feels more wide open than it's been in years.

Just seven games separated No. 1 seed Minnesota from No. 8 New York, while only three games were the difference between No. 4 Atlanta and the top spot.

Then there's Golden State, which nearly finished with the league's best record in just its second season as an expansion franchise, and Washington, which earned the No. 5 seed with the youngest roster in WNBA history. Las Vegas' A'ja Wilson and Jackie Young are chasing their fourth championships, while Chelsea Gray looks to tie the all-time record with her fifth.

There are plenty of fun storylines heading into the postseason, with many teams having a legitimate shot at making a deep run.

Let's run through our predictions for every series, from the first round all the way to the WNBA Finals.

(1) Minnesota Lynx vs. (8) New York Liberty

Congratulations, Minnesota. You went 33-11 on your way to the No. 1 seed. For your efforts, you get to see Breanna Stewart in the first round.

The superstar forward averaged 25.7 points on 55.8 percent shooting from the field against Minnesota this season, winning two of their three matchups.

But Minnesota has been the better team all season, and it does it on both sides of the floor. The Lynx are one of just two teams to rank in the top five in both offensive and defensive rating. With Olivia Miles, Napheesa Collier and Kayla McBride—and coach Cheryl Reeve scheming things up—they present too many challenges for a New York team that isn't as athletic as it was in years past.

New York does have the size to mix up its coverages against Miles, throwing Leonie Fiebich, Breanna Stewart and Jonquel Jones at her. They gave Miles some trouble during the season (32 percent from the field), forcing her to become more of a scorer than a playmaker.

We think New York could steal a game, but it's hard to see the Liberty winning the series unless Sabrina Ionescu goes nuclear from three. She shot under 30 percent from deep for the second straight season and enters the playoffs shooting just 31.3 percent from the field over her last 12 games.

(2) Golden State Valkyries vs. (7) Dallas Wings

This should be a fascinating series. Golden State has undoubtedly been an excellent regular-season team, but how does that translate to playoff basketball? The Valkyries rank No. 7 in offensive rating and don't have an elite shot creator who can consistently bail them out late in games.

Dallas has exactly that in Paige Bueckers, and that gives the Wings a chance in this series. But it's going to take an all-time tough-shot-making masterclass, considering the number of defenders Golden State has to make her life as difficult as possible.

The Wings lost all three regular-season matchups against Golden State and failed to score over 80 points in any of them. Gabby Williams was terrific in those matchups, averaging 22.3 points per game—her most against any opponent. Dallas just doesn't really have any quality wing defenders, especially without Azzi Fudd, who's out for the season with a knee injury.

There are also major worries about Jessica Shepard defensively in this series. The Valkyries do a great job of spreading the floor, forcing switches and creating advantageous positions to attack, which could put Shepard in some uncomfortable spots. Theoretically, you just hide her on Kiah Stokes, but that's easier said than done.

(3) Las Vegas Aces vs. (6) Indiana Fever

There's no doubt this is the most exciting matchup of the first round. A'ja Wilson vs. Aliyah Boston, Chelsea Gray and Jackie Young vs. Caitlin Clark and Kelsey Mitchell, plus the chess match between Becky Hammon and Stephanie White. It's insane that we're getting these teams in the first round. There were scenarios where this could have been a Finals matchup.

These are the two best offensive teams in the league, and two of the best offenses in WNBA history. Indiana has the highest offensive rating of all time, with Las Vegas closely behind them at No. 4.

This series could come down to who gets enough stops when it matters most, and we have more confidence in Las Vegas being able to do that. Indiana has the worst defense among all playoff teams, with some major limitations on the perimeter. How exactly do they keep Jackie Young from getting to the rim whenever she wants? Or deal with those Young-Wilson ball screens?

It could go either way, though. If Indiana gets 55 points per game from Clark and Mitchell, plus an efficient 18 points from Boston, what's stopping them from winning a few shootouts?

(4) Atlanta Dream vs. (5) Washington Mystics

If you love defense and rebounding, this is the series for you. Atlanta and Washington ranked No. 2 and No. 3, respectively, in defensive rating and dominated opponents on the glass more consistently than anyone else in the league, thanks in large part to Angel Reese and Kiki Iriafen.

It's totally possible Washington forces a Game 3 in this series (they have a chance to win it), but Atlanta has more playoff experience and, frankly, more pathways to victory.

The Dream attempt eight more threes per game, giving them a pretty clear advantage in the math battle. So if Rhyne Howard and Allisha Gray catch fire from three, it's hard to see the Mystics keeping up.

And if the shots aren't falling from three, Atlanta can still do enough damage in transition to win an ugly offensive game. Washington has the highest turnover rate in the league, while Atlanta forces more turnovers than any other team.

Shakira Austin's play on both ends will be crucial to Washington's success in this series. She has been on an absolute tear since the All-Star break, averaging over 20 points per game. Austin could also be key to slowing down Angel Reese, who shot just 30.6 percent from two across three matchups against the Mystics—her lowest mark against any opponent.

(1) Minnesota Lynx vs. (4) Atlanta Dream

This could be a really fun series. Minnesota presents some unique challenges for Atlanta with how well it takes care of the ball, creates efficient looks around the rim and keeps opponents off the free-throw line. But Atlanta can create problems of its own with its offensive rebounding and defensive versatility.

In a playoff series, opponents will poke at every limitation you have and try to capitalize on any weakness. That's where some of Atlanta's concerns become more important. The Dream have three starters who aren't reliable shooters, and Minnesota will likely be more than happy to let those players beat them from three.

There are also some questions about Atlanta's rim protection with Bri Jones sidelined for the rest of the season. Opponents shoot 59.8 percent at the rim against the Dream—the lowest mark among all playoff teams—per Synergy Sports.

Atlanta is capable of beating anyone, but as we mentioned earlier, the playoffs are about pathways to success and having multiple ways to win when things don't go your way. Minnesota has the pick-and-roll playmaking, shooting, finishing and defense to make things difficult on Atlanta.

(2) Golden State Valkyries vs. (3) Las Vegas Aces

With all due respect to the Golden State Valkyries, whoever wins the first round between Las Vegas and Indiana will likely be my pick to advance to the Finals. But an Indiana matchup would be more favorable.

I just don't see a way for the Valkyries to score enough points to keep up with the Aces' Big Three. Las Vegas won all three regular-season matchups, and no team averaged more points per game against Golden State this season than the Aces (89.0).

Stokes is obviously Golden State's best option to defend Wilson, but are we sure she'll even be playable offensively in a series where the Valkyries need to score enough points to win? Then you're looking at Janelle Salaün playing small-ball 5 minutes, and, uh, I don't feel great about that either.

We could be looking at a sweep for the Aces, but I hope the Valkyries prove me wrong, though. It sure would be cool if a team without a superstar player made (or even won) the Finals.

(1) Minnesota Lynx vs. (3) Las Vegas Aces

The two best players of the last half decade. The point gawd and the rookie who grew up modeling her game after her. Two of the most efficient perimeter scorers of this era. The two best coaches in the sport.

There would be nothing better than this.

There's a lot of basketball to be played before we get to this series, but at this point, Minnesota's well-rounded roster instills more confidence.

Both teams have the star power, but I sure do feel better about the Lynx's fourth and fifth starters being Courtney Williams and Natasha Howard (two All-Stars), compared to Las Vegas having Bri Turner and Stephanie Talbot.

A rookie starting point guard has never won a WNBA Finals, but nothing about Miles' play screams "rookie." If she doesn't falter in the moment, everything the Lynx do offensively is going to flow through her. When she's picking teams apart in ball screens and creating advantages at will, there's almost no answer.

articles.title: Did Shaquille O’Neal really earn almost $300 million playing basketball?

articles.body:
Shaquille O'Neal earned nearly $300 million

Shaquille O'Neal's NBA salary totaled $292,198,327 across 19 seasons. The figure puts his playing income close to $300 million before counting the businesses and endorsements that extended his earning power beyond the court.

From his 1992 debut with Orlando to his final season with Boston in 2010-11, O'Neal played for 6 teams. His salary total covers his NBA playing career; it does not include endorsement deals, licensing, television work or later business ventures.

Shaquille O'Neal started with $40 million

Orlando selected O'Neal first overall in the 1992 NBA Draft and signed him to a reported seven-year contract worth about $40 million. The agreement made him one of the highest-paid rookies in professional basketball.

His contract allowed him to become a free agent after the 1995-96 season. O'Neal exercised that option in 1996 after four seasons with Orlando, opening the way for his move to Los Angeles .

Los Angeles signed O'Neal to a seven-year contract worth about $120 million in July 1996. Contemporary reporting described the agreement as one of the richest contracts in professional sports at the time.

The Lakers cleared salary-cap space before completing the deal. O'Neal then spent eight seasons in Los Angeles, winning three consecutive NBA championships from 2000 through 2002 alongside Kobe Bryant .

O'Neal's compensation increased sharply during his Lakers years as later contracts replaced the original 1996 agreement. His NBA salary climbed above $23 million per season before he left Los Angeles in 2004.

His Los Angeles tenure included the 2000 NBA MVP award, three Finals MVP awards, and three consecutive championships. Those honors marked the most decorated stretch of O'Neal's 19-season professional basketball career.

O'Neal recorded his highest listed single-season NBA salary at about $27.7 million during the 2004-05 season. His listed pay that year reached $27,696,430, the largest annual salary of his professional career.

He played that season with Miami , averaging 22.9 points and 10.4 rebounds per game. O'Neal finished second in MVP voting before helping the Heat win the franchise's first NBA championship in 2006.

Shaquille O'Neal signs $100 million deal

Miami signed O'Neal to a five-year, $100 million contract in August 2005. He accepted $20 million annually after opting out of a deal that would have paid roughly $30.6 million for the coming season.

The new agreement gave O'Neal long-term security while providing Miami additional salary flexibility. The Heat won the 2006 NBA championship the following season, giving him the fourth and final title of his career.

Shaquille O'Neal still earned $21 million

O'Neal earned $21 million with Cleveland in 2009-10, the fifth-highest NBA player salary listed by ESPN for that season.

His pay fell to about $1.4 million in his final season with Boston in 2010-11. He was 38 when that season began and turned 39 in March 2011, shortly before retiring.

Shaquille O'Neal built Hall of Fame value

O'Neal retired after the 2010-11 season with 28,596 points, 13,099 rebounds, and four NBA championships. He also earned 15 All-Star selections and won the 1993 Rookie of the Year award during his career.

O'Neal entered the Naismith Basketball Hall of Fame in 2016, five years after his final NBA season with Boston. His résumé also included three Finals MVP awards and the 2000 NBA MVP.

O'Neal earned about $292 million in NBA salary, and Forbes estimated that he earned nearly as much from endorsements during his playing career. His basketball pay was only part of his commercial income.

Early sponsors included Reebok, Spalding, trading card companies and toy makers. In 1992, the Los Angeles Times estimated that those initial endorsement deals could be worth up to $30 million, compared with his reported $40 million Orlando contract.

Fun fact: O'Neal said a college professor gave him an F when he pitched a line of Shaq-branded shoes, socks and shirts.

Shaquille O'Neal changed his shoe strategy

O'Neal said a confrontation over expensive sneakers pushed him toward lower-priced footwear. His Shaq and Dunkman brands later sold more than 90 million pairs over roughly 15 years through lower-cost retail channels.

He partnered with companies that sold the shoes through affordable outlets, including Payless. The strategy expanded his business beyond traditional endorsements while giving consumers less expensive alternatives to premium basketball footwear.

In 2016, one estimate suggested O'Neal's partnership with Authentic Brands could generate between $230 million and $270 million over his lifetime. The arrangement expanded the commercial value of his name beyond basketball salary.

Authentic later added Reebok to its portfolio, reconnecting O'Neal with a brand he endorsed as a rookie. His relationship eventually expanded into an executive role focused on the company's basketball operations.

Shaquille O'Neal became a Reebok executive

O'Neal became President of Reebok Basketball in October 2023, adding an executive role to his post-career résumé. The appointment expanded a relationship with the company that first signed him as a rookie in 1992.

His business interests also include Big Chicken, a restaurant brand operating across traditional and nontraditional venues. The company lists locations in 17 states, as well as sites in arenas and on Carnival cruise ships.

"Focus on who is here," Angel Reese responds to A'ja Wilson's Team USA absence , emphasizing attention on the players available rather than those missing from the roster.

Shaquille O'Neal's total reflects longevity

O'Neal played 1,207 regular-season games across 19 NBA seasons, averaging 23.7 points and 10.9 rebounds. His listed playing salary totaled $292,198,327 across 6 teams.

He won 4 championships, 3 Finals MVP awards and 1 regular-season MVP, and earned 15 All-Star selections. His career ran from his Orlando debut in 1992 to his final season with Boston in 2010-11.

articles.title: Los Cavaliers estarán en el Martín Carpena
articles.standfirst: El equipo de Cleveland, que hará una concentración en 'The Embassy', en Fuengirola, harán una exhibición abierta al público el 4 de octubre
articles.summary: El equipo de Cleveland, que hará una concentración en 'The Embassy', en Fuengirola, harán una exhibición abierta al público el 4 de octubre
articles.body: Tras varios días de entrenamiento y preparación en 'The Embassy', en Fuengirola (Málaga), los Cleveland Cavaliers disputarán un scrimmage abierto al público el domingo 4 de octubre, a las 12.00 horas, en el Palacio de Deportes José María Martín Carpena. El encuentro dará la bienvenida a jóvenes jugadores de clubes y academias locales, y ofrecerá a la comunidad del baloncesto malagueño la oportunidad de vivir la NBA de cerca, al tiempo que refuerza el vínculo de los Cavaliers con la ciudad y la región. El scrimmage se organiza en colaboración con The Embassy, el Ayuntamiento de Málaga, la Diputación de Málaga y la delegación malagueña de la Federación Andaluza de Baloncesto (FAB). Las entidades participantes distribuirán 10.000 entradas entre jóvenes de clubes y academias locales para este evento. Antes del scrimmage, los Cavaliers abrirán su Training Camp 2026, presentado por Cleveland Clinic, en The Embassy, en Andalucía, donde el equipo entrenará del 30 de septiembre al 3 de octubre. El campus marcará la primera vez que un equipo de la NBA celebra su training camp en España. Situado en Fuengirola, en la Costa del Sol, The Embassy es un centro de alto rendimiento de baloncesto concebido para este fin y diseñado por José Calderón, exjugador de la Selección Española y actual assistant general manager de los Cavaliers, junto a Berni Rodríguez, también exjugador de la Selección Española. El centro cuenta con aproximadamente 1.500 metros cuadrados de infraestructura profesional de baloncesto, incluidas dos pistas con estándar FIBA/NBA, un gimnasio de alto rendimiento, zonas de rehabilitación y fisioterapia, recursos de recuperación y tecnología audiovisual para el scouting y la preparación táctica. The Embassy ha sido también la sede de entrenamiento de The Sanctuary, el retiro anual de rendimiento en pretemporada organizado por PLYRS UNTD, la marca comercial de la National Basketball Players Association (NBPA). The Sanctuary regresó a Andalucía por quinto año consecutivo en julio y, a lo largo de ese periodo, ha reunido a más de 200 jugadores de la NBA en The Embassy para entrenamientos, sesiones de trabajo y partidos cinco contra cinco. Málaga y Andalucía ofrecen el escenario idóneo para el training camp de los Cavaliers: clima mediterráneo, un entorno deportivo y de bienestar de primer nivel, y la privacidad que necesita un equipo de la NBA para comenzar la temporada 2026-27. Ese entorno permitirá a los Cavaliers centrarse en el entrenamiento, construir la química del equipo y afianzar la camaradería antes de la campaña.

articles.title: LeBron James Wants to Give 'Blueprint' to Joel Embiid, Help Complete 'The Process' with 76ers
articles.summary: Thirteen years after the Philadelphia 76ers entered their "Trust the Process" era, LeBron James is focused on helping the franchise fulfill their ultimate goal by winning an NBA championship.
articles.body:
Thirteen years after the Philadelphia 76ers entered their "Trust the Process" era, LeBron James is focused on helping the franchise fulfill their ultimate goal by winning an NBA championship.

On the latest Mind the Game episode released Friday (starts at 15:45 mark), James explained he wants to give the "blueprint" of what it takes to win at the highest level to Joel Embiid and Tyrese Maxey in order to help the Sixers complete "the process" this season.

10 NBA Players With the Most to Lose at Training Camp 😓

Later in the episode (starts at 20:45 mark), James said Embiid's presence and a desire to help him win influenced his decision to sign with Philadelphia:

"He's done everything in our league. And the only thing he has not done — that's win a championship. And I want to try to help him get that first one. He's been the MVP of our league, has a gold medal, All-Stars, signature shoes, bunch of money, beautiful family. He has everything. He has the city on his back. It's been the process, you know, for what 10 years, 12 years or however long he's been there. But, I mean, I think it's time now that we even dig even deeper into the process, and I hope that I can be kind of that final little piece that can help him get over the hump and maybe just see it a little bit differently than he's seen it in his career, as far as the day-to-day process, the day-to-day what it takes to get there."

articles.title: LeBron James Backs Jaylen Brown, Says He's 'Misunderstood' Ahead of 1st 76ers Season Together
articles.summary: Ahead of his upcoming debut with the Philadelphia 76ers, LeBron James gave his thoughts on new teammate Jaylen Brown and the perception people have of him.
articles.body:
Ahead of his upcoming debut with the Philadelphia 76ers, LeBron James gave his thoughts on new teammate Jaylen Brown and the perception people have of him.

When asked by co-host Steve Nash during the latest episode of their Mind the Game podcast on Friday (beginning at the 24:12 mark) , James explained why he believes Brown is "misunderstood."

10 NBA Players With the Most to Lose at Training Camp 😓

"I just think anytime someone kind of moves to their own beat, it makes people uncomfortable," James said. "He has his own voice. He moves to the sound of his own beat. It makes people uncomfortable because it's not what everyone's accustomed to. When it becomes misunderstood, then it becomes intimidating, and people look at it as 'I don't wanna be around that,' because they feel intimidated by it.

"Am I right? I don't know. I'm gonna spend some time and get an opportunity to be around him even more. We've worked out three or four times this offseason, we've been in communication because we're two of the guys on the team that's been through the foxhole and been through the ringer of what it takes from the moment we step on the court for training camp to the moment when we raise that Larry O'Brien Trophy. We know what it takes. ... It's been nothing but good interaction with JB, and we're gonna continue that."
